page: Microsoft Azure D32pds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine powered by a 3.4 GHz Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. It features 32 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. The system is equipped with 128 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB per core, and a 128 MB L3 cache. It includes a bundled 1890 GB local NVMe SSD and is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core and memory subsystem performance. The server achieves top-tier status in memory bandwidth, reaching 448.6 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 188.32 GB/sec for write operations. Multi-core processing is robust, as evidenced by strong scores in stress-ng multi-core CPU tests, PassMark CPU physics, and Clang software compilation. However, single-core performance and large-scale LLM inference fall into average or poor categories, highlighting a tradeoff where parallelized workloads are favored over raw single-threaded speed.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ARM64 architecture provides a high density of dedicated physical cores and high-speed local NVMe storage without the premium associated with traditional x86 architectures. This resource profile makes the D32pds_v6 highly suitable for database operations, multi-threaded software compilation, static web serving, and general-purpose containerized workloads that benefit from high memory bandwidth and fast local storage.

It is configured with 128 GB of RAM, a 128 MB L3 cache, and a bundled 1890 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server delivers top-tier memory bandwidth, reaching 448.6 GB/sec for large-block reads, alongside strong multi-core performance in software compilation and database operations. While single-core execution and large-scale LLM inference are average, its high memory throughput and fast local storage offer excellent qualitative cost efficiency for parallelized tasks. The D32pds_v6 is highly suited for database hosting, multi-threaded CI/CD pipelines, static web serving, and general-purpose workloads requiring balanced compute and high-speed local storage.
